nodes.label: Cookie Domain Decision (§0)
nodes.rationale: The one decision that dominates everything: get it wrong and login 'succeeds' while every request after it is anonymous. Option A (custom domain, app. and api. on one registrable domain) is same-site: set COOKIE_SAMESITE=lax AND COOKIE_DOMAIN=.pravasisangama.org — the domain is NOT optional and is the part people miss, because without it the API sets a HOST-ONLY cookie bound to api. that middleware.ts on app. cannot read, so login returns 200 and the next navigation 307s back to /login. Same-site governs whether the browser SENDS the cookie; Domain governs which hosts it is SCOPED to; you need both. Option B (vercel.app + onrender.com, both on the Public Suffix List, therefore different sites) forces SameSite=none and is acceptable for staging only — Safari's ITP may drop the cookie and no configuration fixes it from your side, and iPhone is the primary device at this event.

nodes.label: Supabase Connection String Selection
nodes.rationale: Three strings, not interchangeable. Migrations from a laptop use the DIRECT string because DDL runs inside transactions and the runner wraps each file in one. Render runtime uses the SESSION POOLER because it is IPv4 and Render has no guaranteed IPv6 egress while direct connections are IPv6-only on newer projects. The TRANSACTION pooler (:6543) is unusable here because it does not hold a session across statements and withTransaction needs one. Symptom: if the app cannot reach the DB from Render but migrations worked from your laptop, you are on the direct string.

nodes.label: Render Backend Deployment
nodes.rationale: Root Directory must stay at the repository root: this is an npm workspaces monorepo and package-lock.json plus the workspace links live at the root — setting it to backend/ gives a bare package.json whose '@pravasi/shared':'*' dependency resolves against the public registry and fails. build:shared runs before the backend build because shared is consumed as compiled output. build:sql copies schema.sql and migrations into dist/ since tsc only emits JavaScript, making the deployed image self-sufficient. Instance must be Starter or higher: Free instances spin down after ~15 min idle, dropping every dashboard socket and paying a 30-60s cold start, which during an event reads as 'the system is down'. Do not set PORT — Render injects it. app.set('trust proxy', 1) is what makes req.ip reflect the real client for audit logs and rate limiting. If SMTP is unset, production returns 503 EMAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED rather than silently discarding a ticket someone is waiting for.

nodes.label: Vercel Frontend Deployment
nodes.rationale: Root Directory frontend, with 'Include source files outside the Root Directory' ON — that toggle is what lets Vercel see the root package-lock.json and packages/shared; with it off the build fails resolving @pravasi/shared. The explicit build:shared in the build command is belt-and-braces: the package's prepare script builds during install but a cached install can skip it and next build then compiles against a stale dist. NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL INCLUDES /api while NEXT_PUBLIC_SOCKET_URL does NOT, because socket.io appends its own path and namespace. NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are inlined at BUILD time, so changing one requires a redeploy, not a restart. Preview deployments get unique hostnames and will fail CORS against production — correct behaviour; point them at a separate staging Render service rather than widening production's allowlist.

nodes.label: Service Worker No-Cache Headers
nodes.rationale: frontend/vercel.json marks /sw.js and /manifest.json no-cache and /_next/static/* immutable. Without the first rule a CDN-cached service worker keeps serving an old shell after every deploy, and it can persist for a very long time — the worker's job is to survive network loss, which also makes it excellent at surviving your fixes. The static rule is safe because that output is content-hashed.

nodes.label: Forward-Only Migrations and Rollback
nodes.rationale: Migrations are forward-only; there are no down scripts. schema_migrations records what ran, and re-running must log 'skip' on every line — that is what proves the ledger works and a redeploy cannot re-apply DDL. To undo, write a new numbered migration that reverses the change. Restoring a Supabase backup discards every ticket and scan committed since the snapshot, which on event day is almost never the right call. Prefer fixing forward. Frontend rollback is a Vercel Promote to Production (instant, no build); backend is a Render deploy rollback.

nodes.label: Never Run db:seed Against Production
nodes.rationale: The seeder creates superadmin/SuperAdmin@2026 and unit PIN 1234, credentials that are in this repository — running it in production hands anyone with the repo a superuser account and a working gate login. It refuses when NODE_ENV=production, but nothing stops you running it locally POINTED AT the production URL. Create the real superuser instead, generating the bcrypt cost-12 hash locally so the password never leaves your machine, and paste only the hash into the SQL editor.

nodes.label: First-Deploy Order
nodes.rationale: The two services reference each other, so the first deploy needs one circular pass: Supabase (project, migrations, real superuser) -> Render with a placeholder CORS_ORIGIN -> Vercel with the Render URL in both NEXT_PUBLIC_* -> Render with the real CORS_ORIGIN -> custom domains on both, then update CORS_ORIGIN and both NEXT_PUBLIC_* to final hostnames and redeploy each once more.

nodes.label: Ordered Smoke Test
nodes.rationale: Each step depends on the one above; stop at the first failure because the cause is almost always in that step, not later. Health -> CORS -> the ps_session cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, correct SameSite) -> session survives reload -> socket Live pill (grey/Paused means the handshake was rejected, same cookie cause) -> agent login on a real phone -> issue a ticket -> scan it -> airplane-mode PENDING SYNC and drain -> install the PWA.

nodes.label: Before Event Day Checklist
nodes.rationale: Real app icons (install prompts do not appear without 192/512/maskable-512); VENUE_INFO_URL replaced with the real venue map link, since it is currently a placeholder printed on every Normal ticket; Render sized above Free and confirmed not to sleep; Supabase backups enabled with a known restore path; SMTP verified by sending one real ticket or accept the 503; dev seed credentials confirmed absent from production by SQL; a load check of ~200 tickets and a few hundred scans with gate p99 under 50ms; npm audit reviewed.
